https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm2g.text: Figure caption, Watch: President Trump secretly switches planes to avoid Iran threat By Jessica Rawnsley Published 11 August 2026, 09:57 BST Updated 2 hours ago Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month, as part of an elaborate ruse in response to a possible Iranian threat, US media report. The US president boarded Air Force One in view of television cameras before being transported to a military aircraft with the help of a catering truck, the Washington Post said. Journalists and some White House staff on board did not know he had been smuggled out. Officials told the BBC's US partner CBS News that the US had detected a credible Iranian threat to fire a missile at the plane. The White House has not confirmed the secret switch. Trump had earlier said he was Iran's "number one target" during the summit in Ankara. The clandestine manoeuvre came a day after the US renewed military strikes on Iran following a breakdown of negotiations between Washington and Tehran to end the war. Trump had arrived in Turkey aboard a newer Boeing 747-8 donated by Qatar , but announced that he would leave on the old Air Force One "for old time's sake". On 8 July, footage showed him boarding the presidential jet at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president - via a catering truck which had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the C-32A separately using external stairs in an effort to make the flight appear normal, according to the newspaper. Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board. Trump then flew to the UK en route to the US, where he reboarded the old Air Force One and was seen descending from the aircraft after it landed at RAF Mildenhall. It is unclear how he moved from the C-32A back to the legacy jet. Image source, Reuters Image caption, He then boarded the Qatar-gifted jet to fly from the UK to the US The president then transferred to the new Qatari-donated Air Force One to travel back to Washington. During that flight, Trump spoke to reporters on board where he noted the threats posed by Iran but did not mention the earlier plane swap. Asked why reporters had been told to lower the window shades on the plane from Turkey, Trump said: "Because you're probably on a dangerous flight because of the sleazebags we have to deal with." He said he had a "threat all the time" on his life, and that he is "number one" on Iran's "list". "But if I go, you go, right?", he said, adding: "Perhaps someday you want to change professions." Image source, Reuters Image caption, Trump spoke about the threat to him from Iran after boarding the presidential jet given to him by Qatar White House communications director Steven Cheung did not directly confirm or deny the reports, but said the new Air Force One was a "state-of-the-art aircraft" fitted with security measures to protect the president and his staff. US intelligence had previously warned of a specific threat of an attack on Trump or his aircraft, according to earlier reporting by CBS News. The New York Times previously reported on security concerns regarding the Qatari-gifted jet , including that the Secret Service had urged Trump to switch planes on his return from the Nato summit. Several of the publication's journalists were summoned to testify under oath in response. The Justice Department subsequently told the BBC that it was investigating illegal leaks. The US has spent months retrofitting the $400m Boeing 747-8 to prepare it for the president. Older Air Force One planes have laser technology to blind incoming missiles, sources have told CBS News. It is unclear what systems the Qatari jet has. "The new Air Force One is perfectly safe for the President's travels, but will receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete," White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement to CBS News. Chilean penguins fitted with vests to protect healing wounds Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 03/09/2026 - 16:31 GMT+2 Injured Humboldt penguins in Chile are fitted with recovery vests designed to protect wounds and prevent them from damaging stitches as they heal. … More Care in the community has a very particular meaning for penguins in Chile. Injured Humboldt penguins are being fitted with specially designed recovery vests to protect wounds as they heal. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The footage shows handlers checking and measuring the fit, while penguins at a rescue centre walk and rest by a pool wearing the vests. The short-term vests are designed to stop penguins from pecking at wounds or pulling out stitches. Their fabric contains copper and zinc, which can help limit the growth of bacteria and fungi while supporting the healing process. The project remains experimental, with the design adapted to the birds' size and shape. Early trials suggest the penguins tolerate the vests well, and the garments appear to protect wounds during recovery. https://www.dw.com/en/man-injured-after-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5O1CJ New York leaders are demanding answers from the federal government after the shooting Image: Charly Triballeau/AFP Advertisement A man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent during an arrest in New York City, US federal authorities and Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday. The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. local time (2100 GMT) in the Marble Hill neighborhood of Manhattan. The New York Police Department said its officers were not involved in the incident and that the man was conscious and receiving medical attention at a nearby hospital. US President Donald Trump's administration has scaled up ICE raids in major US cities to detain and deport people who are in the US illegally. Protesters slammed the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown Image: Charly Triballeau/AFP Mamdani urges Trump to end ICE actions in NYC New York City Mayor Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he had contacted President Trump . Mamdani added that a five-year-old child was reportedly in the car during the shooting, but that the child was "physically unharmed." "This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said in a post on X. "I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities." New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had spoken with Trump and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin about the shooting. DHS is the parent agency of ICE. "I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York," Hochul said. "I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth." Federal govt says 'criminal illegal alien' in hospital receiving treatment In a post on X, DHS had confirmed that an "ICE officer discharged his weapon" during an attempt to arrest a "criminal illegal alien from the Dominican Republic" with ties "to the Trinitarios gang." DHS said the man had a prior conviction for grand larceny and had been arrested "multiple" times for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession. DHS noted ICE officers immediately rendered aid after the man was injured. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital," the statement said, adding that the FBI was on the scene. Democrat hopeful for the US House, Darializa Avila Chevalier (center-left), joined a rally outside the hospital where the man was being treated Image: Eduardo Munoz/REUTERS ICE, CBP fatal shootings raise alarm in second Trump term Deadly ICE and Border Patrol shootings have drawn major controversy during Trump's second term, particularly regarding the training and oversight of the agents. An ICE agent killed a 37-year-old US citizen, Renee Good , during their operations in Minneapolis in January, triggering demonstrations there and in several other US cities. Later that month, Alex Pretti, another US citizen, was killed by two US Customs and Border Protection officers agents in Minneapolis following an altercation. Europe Taiwan Warns Europe Against China Dependence, Offers Industrial Partnership Taiwan’s foreign minister urged Europe to reduce reliance on Chinese manufacturing, citing semiconductor investments and a planned technology park in Poland. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung delivers a speech at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland on Oct. 13, 2026. Courtesy of Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs Arthur Zhang 10/13/2026 | Updated: 10/13/2026 0:00 X 1 Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung warned European countries on Oct. 13 that dependence on Chinese manufacturing threatens their economic security and political freedom, urging closer industrial cooperation with Taiwan as Europe seeks to reduce its reliance on Beijing. Speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, Lin accused Beijing of using state subsidies and unfair trade practices to undercut European industries and make the continent dependent on Chinese suppliers. “Because China’s authoritarian ideology is fundamentally incompatible with Europe’s democracy, dependence on China is not merely an economic risk. It’s a threat to European freedom and sovereignty itself,” Lin said. “A Europe controlled through its supply chains would be a Europe that had surrendered part of its liberty,” he added. Lin compared Europe’s dependence on Chinese manufacturing with its previous reliance on Russian energy, which became a major vulnerability following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. He warned of what he called “China Shock 2.0,” describing a new wave of Chinese electric vehicles, batteries, solar panels, and steel entering international markets with substantial state support. Related Stories Taiwan President Says Island’s Defense Is Test of Global Rules Amid China Pressure Taiwan Experts Say Trump-Xi Summit Did Not Alter US-China Strategic Divide Lin accused Beijing of using industrial subsidies and below-cost sales to capture markets, weaken European competitors, and make Europe dependent on Chinese suppliers. Europe’s Dependence on China Lin’s remarks came two days before European Union leaders were scheduled to meet in Brussels to discuss economic competitiveness and global trade imbalances affecting European industry. The European Commission has identified China’s industrial subsidies, trade practices, and export restrictions as challenges for European manufacturers. According to the commission, the EU recorded a goods trade deficit of 359.9 billion euros ($403 billion) with China in 2025. European imports from China totaled 559.5 billion euros ($626 billion), compared with 199.5 billion euros ($223 billion) in exports, using Oct. 13 exchange rates. The commission also said Chinese export restrictions on critical raw materials and certain technologies were negatively affecting European supply chains. Its stated policy is to reduce critical dependencies rather than sever economic ties with China. Lin argued that Europe could strengthen its industries by combining its expertise in machinery, automotive engineering, chemicals, and design with Taiwan’s semiconductor manufacturing and electronics supply chains. “Taiwan does not ask Europe to trade one dependence for another,” he said. “We are standing with Europe as a partner it can truly trust.” Taiwanese Investment in Europe Lin cited several Taiwanese semiconductor investments in Europe, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company’s chipmaking project in Germany, GlobalWafers’ investment in Italy, and Foxconn’s advanced chip-packaging project in France. He described the investments as examples of what he called the “Taiwan Model,” which emphasizes cooperation based on democratic values, the rule of law, free markets, and complementary industrial strengths. “Taiwanese investment does not come to hollow out European industries,” he said. “It comes to build alongside it.” Lin also pointed to a planned technology park in southwestern Poland as a further step in Taiwan’s European industrial expansion. On Oct. 12, he visited Miekinia, near Wroclaw, to inspect the proposed site of the TEEMA Technology Park, a project led by the Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers’ Association. The planned park would bring Taiwanese and Polish businesses together in artificial intelligence, smart-city technology, electric vehicles, and advanced manufacturing. Taiwanese Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung (C) poses with Taiwanese and Polish representatives during a visit to the proposed TEEMA Technology Park site in Miekinia, Poland, on Oct. 12, 2026. Taiwan and Poland plan to establish an industrial hub focused on artificial intelligence, smart-city technologies, and electric vehicles. Courtesy of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Taiwan Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry said representatives of Taiwan and Poland intend to sign a memorandum of understanding before the end of 2026, with Taiwan’s International Cooperation and Development Fund helping advance arrangements to secure land. Poland’s Ministry of Economic Development and Technology has also backed the project, describing the proposed park as a platform for cooperation among Taiwanese investors, Polish businesses, universities, and research institutions. Polish Deputy Minister Michal Jaros said in June that Poland was ready to work with Taiwan to build more resilient supply chains. Lin also connected the project to Ukraine’s eventual reconstruction. He said the planned technology park could provide an industrial base for cooperation in artificial intelligence, electric vehicles, and smart-city technologies. “It can become a foundation on which Taiwan contributes to European efforts to reconstruct Ukraine,” Lin said. https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/13/azer.text: Azerbaijan is set to increase and diversify its energy supplies to Europe, beyond the current 10 EU member states, president Ilham Aliyev announced on Thursday during the 9th European Political Community Summit in Dublin.Aliyev held talks with European Council President Antonio Costa during the EPC summit to discuss the long-term energy contracts “in the context of continuing successful cooperation between Azerbaijan and the European Union in gas supplies,” an Azerbaijani presidency statement said, while Costa declared that “the resumption of negotiations on a new EU-Azerbaijan agreement is good news for our citizens.” The EU-Azerbaijan Strategic Partnership in the Field of Energy was established in 2022.Commenting on the meeting, Costa emphasized the two-way benefits of the EU-Azerbaijan cooperation declaring that “this has been an important year for EU-Azerbaijan relations,” adding that “with peace between Azerbaijan and Armenia now a reality, the EU is also investing to ensure that people across the region benefit.”Aliyev said that Azerbaijan increased its gas supplies to the European Union from 8 billion cubic meters to 13 billion cubic meters, which accounts for nearly half of Azerbaijan’s exports, and that with the discovery of new fields, the South Caucasus country plans to increase gas supplies further.The cooperation is now also focusing on renewable energy, a strategic national objective for Azerbaijan, with Aliyev highlighting the agreement reached between Azerbaijan, Georgia, Turkey and Bulgaria on exporting renewable energy to the European markets.Azerbaijan’s president said that the gas pipeline stretching from Baku to Italy, passing through the territories of seven countries and supplying 10 European Union member states via interconnectors in Bulgaria, was currently operating at full capacity, and that Baku intends to continue expanding its transported volumes.Costa and Aliyev also said that the European Union’s assessment of the Nakhchivan railway project would be completed soon and that they discussed the developments of transport links and connectivity within the global Middle Corridor project connecting Asia to Europe through the South Caucasus and Central Asia towards the Black Sea, a fast-developing alternative to the Strait of Hormuz crisis for the global supply lines.Costa invited Aliyev to Brussels to continue the discussions on EU-Azerbaijan’s cooperation given the South Caucasus country’s role in Europe’s energy supply and security.Strategic partnership with the UKAzerbaijan’s president Ilham Aliyev and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham signed a Joint Declaration on Strategic Partnership between Azerbaijan and the United Kingdom, during the EPC Summit in Dublin.With the UK being the largest European investor in Azerbaijan’s economy, historically driven by BP's Caspian operations, the new strategic framework focuses on defence and security cooperation, expanding trade and investment, renewable energy, infrastructure as well as artificial intelligence, advanced technology and others.British officials said relations have now reached a historic milestone and both leaders committed to expanding mutual trade, defence cooperation, and private-sector investment ties under the new accord. With Russia watching on, the UK and Azerbaijan agreed to “strengthening cooperation in defence and security in support of regional peace and stability” (...) “across a broad spectrum of security priorities, in response to evolving security challenges and threats.”The two sides also agreed to “support the development of the Middle Corridor, alongside transport, logistics and infrastructure projects that facilitate cross-border trade and investment.”Securing the Ukrainian grid and drone agreementsUkrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a “detailed discussion” with President Aliyev during the EPC summit, focusing on emergency support for Ukraine's battered energy grid ahead of the harsh winter and post-conflict reconstruction strategies.Zelenskyy confirmed that contracts were signed under the so-called “Drone Deal,” an ongoing bilateral drone agreement, saying that “we are working to scale up orders,” adding that “relations between our countries are developing.”Zelenskyy also thanked Aliyev for Azerbaijan's humanitarian assistance as officials confirmed an ongoing €1.35 million emergency grid support package from Baku, comprising heavy electrical equipment and generators. Total Azerbaijani humanitarian aid to Ukraine has now reached €48 million, focusing on civilian energy infrastructure and medical rehabilitation. Ukraine’s president also noted that Kyiv is closely analysing Azerbaijan's post-conflict reconstruction across Karabakh and the East Zangezur regions, as the Ukrainian government views Baku's massive infrastructural overhaul as a viable blueprint for its own eventual post-war recovery.The two leaders also discussed expanding economic and trade relations, including private-sector economic cooperation, with Zelenskyy saying that “we value the fact that companies are staying and continuing to work for our people, often despite Russia’s vile attacks.”Advancing the Armenia-Azerbaijan peace processBuilding on their historic peace process, Azerbaijan’s president Ilham Aliyev held new talks with Armenian prime minister Nikol Pashinyan on advancing their peace consolidation, border delimitations, water cooperation and interconnection of electricity grids as well as more confidence-building measures.The two leaders also discussed the progress of the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) connectivity project, including the planning of its railway and highway components.Since November 2025, a total of 105,000 tonnes of cargo have been transported to Armenia through the territory of Azerbaijan.Broadening European engagementPresident Aliyev met with Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis for talks on upgrading the Southern Gas Corridor's infrastructure in the context of Azerbaijani-Greek bilateral relations, anchored by the Trans Adriatic Pipeline (TAP). Aliyev also held talks with Moldovan President Maia Sandu on energy cooperation and on strengthening Moldova’s energy security as well as economic and trade ties with a particular focus on the agricultural sector.Azerbaijan’s president met his Romanian counterpart Nicusor Dan for the first time to discuss energy and connectivity projects, focusing on linking the Caspian and the Black Seas.Dan said in a post on X that “we focused on deepening our Strategic Partnership, advancing key energy and connectivity projects, and pursuing an ambitious shared political and economic agenda,” adding that “our cooperation, linking the Caspian and the Black Sea, has strong potential to grow.”Aliyev also held energy talks with Bulgaria’s prime minister Rumen Radev and Czech prime minister Andrej Babis.
